reset-confirm-desc: The settings you have configured will not be kept after the reset.
encoder-tip: Click the icon to get, Right-click the icon to test
folder-tip: Click the icon to select, Right-click the icon to open
appendant-path-tip: Put the skin packs and material packs you downloaded here (zips as-is, no need to extract)
log-path-tip: Every run is recorded here (one file per day); exported logs go here too
print-stderr-tip: Display rendering output in the main terminal
enable-play-button-tip: Show the "Play" button on the render page to play the chart in-game
preview-fullscreen-tip: Open the preview / play / offset-tweak window fullscreen. Turn off to run it windowed.
list-expand-tip: Right-click the sidebar to switch at any time
show-debug-tip: Shows the Test and Debug sections on the render page
high-performance-tip: Lets the GPU do as much as possible: prefers the discrete GPU and flips the frame on the GPU (speed only)
strip-width-tip: Width of the render panel at the bottom right, as a percentage of the content area (15–100)
about-intro: A Windows desktop app that renders Phigros charts into videos offline: a Tauri 2 shell, a Vue 3 frontend and an embedded Rust rhythm-game engine (DPS) that parses the chart, runs the judgement and draws every frame.
about-thanks: HLMC and Mivik (authors of Phi-Recorder); TeamFlos and its contributors (Phira, phira-render); the maintainers of Phira-Pro; and every open-source author whose work this repository uses, directly or indirectly.
about-projects-tip: The upstream and reference implementations this project builds on (click to open in your browser):
about-proj-phire: The same author's Phira-lineage project, direct upstream of DPS
about-proj-phira-pro: A modified Phira, source of the block-area implementation
about-proj-phi-recorder: Direct upstream of DPR (a fork of phira-render)

about-ai: This project was developed with assistance from DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (DeepSeek official API, model id deepseek-flash): much of the code, documentation, refactoring and integration came out of human-AI collaboration, with the human author setting requirements, making decisions and validating the results. Model output can be wrong — the code in the repository and real measurements win.
